question: What is the clinical definition of a bone fracture?

options.A: A severe stretching of the ligaments around a joint
options.B: An infection located deep inside the bone marrow
options.C: A complete break or disruption in bone continuity
options.D: A complete wearing away of the cartilage at a joint

explanation: A fracture is simply a break in the normal continuity of the bone structure caused by excessive force. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman with poor calcium intake suffer a fracture from a very minor fall?

options.A: Her bones have lost structural strength and cannot absorb normal impact
options.B: Her joints swell up so much that the bone pops out of place
options.C: Her blood circulation completely stops inside the arms and legs
options.D: Her muscles pull so tightly that they snap the healthy bone in half

explanation: Poor mineral density weakens bones, lowering the threshold of force needed to cause a break. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h1)

question: Which fracture type involves the broken bone piercing through the external skin?
explanation: An open or compound fracture breaks through the skin surface, exposing internal tissues to the outside environment. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h2)

question: A two-year-old child falls and sustains a partial break where the bone bends and cracks on one side only. What is this called?
explanation: Children have softer, more pliable bones that tend to bend and break partially rather than snapping completely, like a fresh green tree branch. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h2)

question: What is formed in the fracture gap during the very first days after a bone breaks?

options.A: A fibrous band of mature scar muscle tissue
options.B: A thick layer of flexible articular cartilage
options.C: A hard sheet of dense cortical bone tissue
options.D: A blood clot known as a fracture hematoma

explanation: Vessel damage at the injury site immediately causes bleeding, creating a localized blood clot that starts the healing cascade. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h3)

question: What primary cellular action occurs during the final stage of bone remodeling?

options.A: Osteoclasts clean up excess bone tissue while osteoblasts rebuild compact bone
options.B: Skin cells grow inward to close the gap left by the broken bone ends
options.C: Red blood cells multiply rapidly to replace lost marrow volume
options.D: Fibroblasts convert the entire shaft into soft flexible cartilage permanently

explanation: Remodeling requires a balance where old or excess bone is cleared away and strong bone is shaped along stress lines. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h3)

question: What is the clinical term for the grating sound or feel when broken bone ends rub together?
explanation: Crepitus occurs when rough fractured bone surfaces grind against one another during movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h4)

question: Why must a midwife check capillary refill and pulse distal to a suspected fracture site?

options.A: To calculate the exact amount of pain medication the patient needs
options.B: To see if the patient has an underlying systemic blood infection
options.C: To make sure blood flow and nerve function are not cut off
options.D: To determine how long the bone will take to form a hard callus

explanation: Displaced bone fragments can easily compress or damage major blood vessels and nerves running down the limb. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of applying a splint to a broken limb during emergency care?

options.A: To speed up the immediate cellular remodeling phase of healing
options.B: To force a crooked bone completely back into a straight alignment
options.C: To completely eliminate all sensation of pain in the injured limb
options.D: To prevent further injury to surrounding blood vessels and nerves

explanation: Immobilization stops sharp bone ends from moving around and tearing nearby soft tissues, blood vessels, or nerves. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h5)

question: When applying a temporary splint to a patient with a fractured lower leg bone, which joints must be secured?

options.A: The joints immediately above and below the fracture site
options.B: All joints located in both the upper and lower body extremities
options.C: Only the single joint closest to the site of the actual break
options.D: Only the joint at the very end of the toes and the hip joint

explanation: To truly immobilize a fractured bone shaft, the joints on both ends must be locked to prevent rotational or bending movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h5)

question: What does the abbreviation ORIF stand for in orthopedic fracture management?
explanation: ORIF refers to surgically opening the site to reduce the fracture and placing internal hardware like plates and screws. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h6)

question: When is an external fixation device typically chosen over internal plates and screws?

options.A: When the bone has already completed its final remodeling phase
options.B: When severe open fractures have extensive soft tissue damage and infection risk
options.C: When the fracture is a simple, closed, transverse break in a child
options.D: When the patient refuses to take any form of oral pain medication

explanation: External frames keep metal away from contaminated open wounds while holding complex, unstable fragments securely in place. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h6)

question: Which complication involves dangerously high pressure inside an enclosed muscle space cutting off blood supply?
explanation: Swelling inside rigid fascial compartments cuts off blood flow, causing intense pain and potential permanent tissue damage if untreated. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h7)

question: What is a hallmark clinical sign of compartment syndrome that distinguishes it from normal fracture pain?

options.A: Severe pain that does not go away even after giving strong pain medication
options.B: Sudden cooling of the skin temperature in the toes of the uninjured leg
options.C: The appearance of bright red bruising spreading outward across the chest
options.D: A complete absence of any swelling or puffiness around the broken bone

explanation: Unrelenting pain unresponsive to analgesics is a classic red flag for rising pressure cutting off tissue perfusion. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h7)
